blockers.title: Admin recipe editor shows 1000x costs when recipe unit differs from catalog unit
blockers.detail: Both compute qty * rate with no unit conversion. qty is in the recipe unit (g), rate is per catalog unit (kg). West Coast IPA editor shows Totals $6,059.66/$13,809.97 for a recipe selling at $93.73. Correct math gives $23.32/$43.75 -> +$45 service +$5 materials = $93.75 vs $93.73 charged.
blockers.customer_impact: NONE - middleware converts correctly, customers are not overcharged. Display-only.
blockers.scope: 20 hop rows stored in g across 7 recipes, plus gypsum and calcium chloride. Grain is kg in both places so grain rows look correct.
blockers.recommendation: Fix the code, leave the data. Normalising hops to kg would make the editor appear correct while hiding the bug. Needs its own plan plus regression test.

blockers.title: Deployment config contradicts documentation
blockers.detail: Live is 'Execute as: Me' + 'Who has access: Anyone'; docs/APPS_SCRIPT.md and adminApi.gs's own header say it MUST be 'User accessing the web app' + 'Anyone with Google Account'. Session.getActiveUser().getEmail() returns empty, making that limb of checkAuthorization dead code in production. NOT an open endpoint - the OAuth-token path and server-token bypass both work.

blockers.title: Admin swallows the unit_mismatch error and the unit is not editable
blockers.detail: Middleware returns a precise 422 (code: unit_mismatch, cause: the ingredient name); the UI shows only 'Could not save recipe. Please try again', which invites a retry that can never work. The unit renders as plain text (td.ing-unit), not an input - the only repair path is re-picking the ingredient from the autocomplete, which silently resyncs the unit from the catalog.
